features.title: Supabase reader: tables and RLS policies from SQL migrations

acceptance.check: Migrations are applied in file order like Postgres: DROP TABLE removes the table and its policies, CREATE TABLE after DROP starts fresh (new columns, RLS off), ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO / SET SCHEMA moves the table and its policies, DROP POLICY removes the policy, and ALTER POLICY changes only the USING, WITH CHECK or roles it names

Each policy is reported as permissive or restrictive (AS RESTRICTIVE), and db_policies stores it as a flag; a restrictive policy never counts as allowing everyone (db_policies rejects allows_all = true on a restrictive policy)

A table touched by a statement that cannot be parsed (syntax error, unterminated string) or followed (dynamic SQL in a DO block that changes RLS or policies) is reported with RLS unknown (rlsUnknown true, rlsEnabled false), never enabled; unparseable statements are in errors[] with file and line, and a later explicit ENABLE/DISABLE makes the state known again
